original_question: For every red-blue colouring of the edges of the hypercube Q_n, determine whether there must exist a path between some antipodal pair of vertices that changes colour only o(n) times.
target_in_paper: Section 8, Question 8.2 (posed as a step toward Conjecture 8.1 in “Antipodal paths in Q_n with few colour changes”).
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly identifies the ambient graph Q_n, uses a red-blue edge-colouring, asks for existence of a path between some antipodal pair of vertices, and uses the asymptotic threshold o(n) colour-changes. Just as importantly, it does not accidentally strengthen the problem to the geodesic/one-switch statement of Conjecture 8.1, and it does not drift into the averaged variant of Question 8.3.
missing_details: Define Q_n explicitly as the n-dimensional hypercube with vertex set {0,1}^n and edges joining pairs of vertices that differ in exactly one coordinate.
Define antipodal vertices explicitly: x and y are antipodal if they differ in every coordinate, equivalently y is the bitwise complement of x.
Specify what a colour-change on a path means: a position where two consecutive edges of the path receive different colours.

Make the asymptotic meaning of o(n) fully explicit, e.g. by asking for a function f(n)=o(n) bounding the number of colour-changes, or equivalently using the quantifier form “for every epsilon > 0, for all sufficiently large n”.
Clarify that the path is not required to be geodesic or shortest; this is essential because the stronger geodesic one-switch statement is Conjecture 8.1, not Question 8.2.
State the quantifiers in stand-alone form: for every n and every red-blue colouring of E(Q_n), there should exist some antipodal pair and a path between them meeting the bound.
refined_question: Let Q_n be the n-dimensional hypercube with vertex set {0,1}^n and edges joining pairs of vertices that differ in exactly one coordinate. Two vertices are called antipodal if they differ in every coordinate. Is there a function f(n)=o(n) such that, for every n and every red-blue colouring of the edges of Q_n, there exist antipodal vertices x and y joined by an x-y path P for which the number of indices i at which the i-th and (i+1)-st edges of P have different colours is at most f(n)?
justification: The nearest official formulation is Question 8.2, not Conjecture 8.1. Section 8 first states the stronger Leader-Long conjecture that there should be a geodesic antipodal path with at most one colour-change, and then says “As a step towards this Conjecture ... Question 8.2,” whose exact wording is the o(n)-colour-change path version. The surrounding context defines the stronger geodesic problem, explains what “geodesic” means, and records the known upper bounds n/2 and then (3/8+o(1))n, confirming that Question 8.2 is precisely the asymptotic path problem your draft is aiming at. Question 8.3 is a different averaged variant over a randomly chosen antipodal pair, so your draft should not be rewritten in that direction. The refinement therefore keeps your scope but makes the notation, antipodality, colour-change count, and asymptotic quantifiers fully explicit.
